findings.classification: source-backed conditional bearing-contact policy and graph-reachability question; central reconciliation decides count and alias
findings.first_contract: audit_positive_bearing claims physical interfaces overlap their owning solid including full rotation but tests selected frame/heating/workplace roles with oriented cuboid overlap and tests other roles, including RoofEdgeTreatment and RoofGutter, with a yaw-only bounds overlap. The fallback disregards crossfall and longfall. Same owner and supported node plus any overlapping interface suffice.
findings.conditions: If a representable roof-role solid/interface pair reaches this audit with yaw-only overlap above 0.001 m but no actual oriented physical overlap, and physical contact is required for that role, the local bearing predicate can refrain from reporting missing_positive_bearing. Full graph admission, supported producer reachability, all other audit issues and intended tolerance/shape policy are not established.
findings.symbolic_reasoning_only: Consider a 2 m x 0.07 m x 0.14 m cuboid at centre (0,0,0), yaw/crossfall 0 and longfall 45 degrees, with a matching-owner and matching-node interface centred (0.8,0,0) and half-extents (0.08,0.025,0.08). The yaw-only proxy spans x ±1, y ±0.035, z ±0.07, so all axis overlaps exceed 0.001. Under inverse Z rotation every point in the interface has local y at most (0.025 - 0.72)/sqrt(2), below -0.49 m, outside the solid y half-size 0.035 m: the pair does not physically intersect. This is mathematical reasoning on source expressions only, not a constructed or executed fixture, accepted state, current output or evidence this exact interface is generated.
findings.producer_context: The actual weathering producer assigns RoofEdgeTreatment to non-eave edge solids and computes their nonzero longfall from edge pitch; it creates a support interface at the edge midpoint with the same owner and first support node. That demonstrates relevant rotation-bearing source shape, but not this hypothetical displacement or any complete reachable successful plan.
